# ACC008 `timer-without-acc-wait`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A timer is read while asynchronous OpenACC work may still be running.

## Why

`async` compute and data constructs return immediately: reading the clock right after them
measures only the launch, not the work. Put `!$acc wait` (or `call acc_wait(...)`) before every
stop-time read.

## Reported

```fortran
!$acc parallel loop async(1)
...
call system_clock(t1)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
!$acc parallel loop async(1)
...
!$acc wait
call system_clock(t1)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC008] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC008` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
